purpose: Qualitatively different implementation holdout for the closed-form/boundary-BDD upper-Shapley certifier. This is not a new estimator-selection experiment and does not authorize lemma-library policy changes.

games.construction: For each seed, uniformly permute players with random.Random(seed). The first 8 form core C and the last 2 are tail t0,t1. Let q=3+(seed mod 2). The game is true iff |S intersect C|>=q OR bridge1 subset S OR bridge2 subset S. bridge1={C[0],t0,t1}; bridge2={C[1],C[2],t0}. This differs structurally from the prior random small-antichain generator by including a large symmetric threshold family plus sparse exception supports.

primary_endpoint: maximum absolute numerical difference across all game/player/budget cells
pass_condition: all three methods agree within 1e-12 in every cell
secondary_endpoints: maximal b-slice zero boundary clause count
minimal a-slice one boundary clause count
scope: Implementation/parity holdout only. Synthetic monotone simple games; no claim about nonmonotone finite-compute proof utility.
